turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Aoife, in you come. What's brought you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Contraception, basically. I want to get sorted with contraception. The bus was a pure mess, some fella's wheelie case jammed in the door the whole way from town.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And I wasn't sitting in the car for that.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): You could have, mam. Anyway the last pill did not agree with me at all.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which one.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm it was microginon. That's the one. I stopped it.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did you stop.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Err I can't date it. Sometime in the spring, I think, but I honestly don't know.
[SEG0009] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She was plagued with headaches the whole time she took it.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah they were brutal, behind the eyes, the whole time I was on it. They've gone since I stopped. I'm not getting them now.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any headache today.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm only the odd cigarette, two or three at the weekend if we're out. Not daily. Sinead from work smokes a lot more, but that's her own business.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Asthma is on your form.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah I've had asthma since I was about seven. It's mostly grand.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cough.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Never.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Phlegm.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that either.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Wheeze.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes, if I'm legging it for the bus.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Waking at night with the asthma.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's tired all the time though. Falls asleep on the couch the minute she sits down.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I am not tired. I'm grand. That was one night after a late shift, mam, not all the time.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Inhaler and dose.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Just the blue ventalin for the asthma, when I need it. A hundred micrograms.
[SEG0031] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The nurse read that box as two hundred micrograms. I was standing there.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): She did not. It's a hundred. You were in talking to her about your own tablets, not mine.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Periods painful.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Not painful, no. Regular enough. I was going to tell you about the Galway wedding but sure that's nothing to do with it.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chance you're pregnant.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Flashing lights with those old headaches.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Never.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any trouble with the waterworks.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not a bother.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Drug reactions. Any.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm I'm not sure. Years ago I got a rash and I went all puffy, but maybe it was the antibiotic or the painkiller. Nobody told me which.
[SEG0043] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I still think it was the penicillin they gave her for the throat.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): That's a guess, mam. I still don't know if it was the antibiotic or the painkiller.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure is 118 over 74.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that grand? In college they said it was on the low side. I can't remember the figure. Different thing anyway.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's fine for today. Provisionally I'd say the combined pill doesn't suit you, between those headaches and the smoking.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. So what are the actual options. My cousin has the implant and she says it's deadly, though she brings it up at every dinner which is a bit much.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Progesterone-only pill, implant, or a coil. I'd favour the implant. No tablet to start today.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): The coil I'm not mad on, and I won't remember a pill. Can I have something to read on the implant.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): There's the implant leaflet. Come back in three weeks and tell me what you've decided.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks, yeah. And the odd cigarette, do I have to knock them on the head.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes if you can. It doesn't change the plan for today.

spec.situation: Young woman asks about contraception, previous pill caused headaches, smokes occasionally; blood pressure read; options discussed; implant leaflet given, decision next visit.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

bad.reason: Patient says 'Not really,' not a definite absent cough.
